question: Should OpenClaw make `resetToken` a supported generic agent-harness and plugin session-end correlation field, or should this retained-reset correlation move behind a narrower owner-controlled seam?
rationale: The implementation is additive and appears correct for Codex, but it changes a shared lifecycle contract whose future plugin and harness semantics cannot be inferred safely from this one repair.

options.title: Confirm the generic correlation field
options.body: Accept the additive transient field as a generic lifecycle correlation mechanism and land the PR with its current exact-token fencing.

options.title: Narrow the ownership boundary
options.body: Redesign the handoff so retained-reset correlation remains inside a core-owned or Codex-specific seam rather than the shared plugin lifecycle event.

options.title: Pause for lifecycle API design
options.body: Defer the PR until maintainers define broader lifecycle-correlation requirements for multiple harnesses and plugins.

recommendation.title: Confirm the generic correlation field
recommendation.body: Accept the additive transient field as a generic lifecycle correlation mechanism and land the PR with its current exact-token fencing.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the retained-session reset design that changed the lifecycle invariant at issue.
